drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: Which joint, bone, or muscle is bothering you, and what is the main problem: pain, swelling, stiffness, weakness, or trouble moving it?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the location and main complaint guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: Did this start after an injury, fall, or twisting movement? What happened?
questions.rationale: Mechanism of injury guides fracture and ligament assessment.

questions.text: Can you put weight on the leg or use the arm normally, or is it too painful?
questions.rationale: Inability to bear weight or use the limb after injury suggests fracture or severe sprain.

questions.text: Does the limb look misshapen, or did you hear or feel a pop or snap?
questions.rationale: Visible deformity or a pop points to fracture, dislocation, or tendon/ligament rupture.

questions.text: When did this start, and is it getting better, worse, or staying the same?
questions.rationale: Onset and course distinguish acute injury from chronic or inflammatory conditions.

questions.text: How would you describe the pain: sharp, aching, burning, throbbing? What makes it better or worse?
questions.rationale: Pain quality and triggers help separate mechanical from inflammatory or neuropathic pain.

questions.text: Is the area swollen, red, or warm to the touch?
questions.rationale: Swelling with warmth and redness suggests inflammation or infection.

questions.text: Is one joint hot, swollen, and very painful, and have you had fever or chills?
questions.rationale: A hot swollen joint with fever may be septic arthritis, which needs urgent treatment.

questions.text: Are you stiff in the morning, and for how long does the stiffness last?
questions.rationale: Prolonged morning stiffness (over 30 to 60 minutes) suggests inflammatory arthritis.

questions.text: Are other joints affected, and does the pain move from joint to joint or affect both sides?
questions.rationale: Joint distribution helps separate osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, and viral causes.

questions.text: Does the joint lock, catch, or give way?
questions.rationale: Mechanical symptoms suggest meniscal tear, loose body, or ligament injury.

questions.text: Do you have numbness, tingling, or weakness in the arm or leg?
questions.rationale: Neurologic symptoms may indicate nerve root or peripheral nerve involvement.

questions.text: Do you have numbness between your legs or around the saddle area, new trouble controlling urine or stool, or both legs weak?
questions.rationale: These are signs of cauda equina syndrome, a surgical emergency.

questions.text: Does the pain wake you at night or stay present when you are resting?
questions.rationale: Constant night or rest pain raises concern for infection, tumor, or inflammation.

questions.text: Have you had unintended weight loss, or a history of cancer?
questions.rationale: Back or bone pain with cancer history or weight loss raises concern for metastasis.

questions.text: Is the limb cold, pale, or numb, or have you lost the pulse or color in it?
questions.rationale: A pulseless, pale, or cold limb suggests vascular compromise.

questions.text: Is one calf swollen, tender, or warm?
questions.rationale: Unilateral calf findings raise concern for deep vein thrombosis.

questions.text: Have you recently changed your exercise, work tasks, or repetitive activities?
questions.rationale: Overuse and training errors are common causes of tendinopathy and stress injury.

questions.text: Have you injured or had surgery on this area before?
questions.rationale: Prior injury raises the chance of recurrence or degenerative change.

questions.text: Do you have a rash, psoriasis, red or painful eyes, or bowel symptoms like diarrhea?
questions.rationale: Extra-articular features suggest spondyloarthritis or reactive arthritis.

questions.text: Does anyone in your family have rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, psoriasis, or gout?
questions.rationale: Family history raises likelihood of autoimmune or crystal arthritis.

questions.text: Do you take steroids, statins, fluoroquinolone antibiotics, or diuretics, or have you started anything new?
questions.rationale: These medicines are linked to tendon injury, myopathy, or gout flares.

questions.text: Have you had falls, fractures from minor injury, or been told you have osteoporosis?
questions.rationale: Fragility fractures suggest low bone density.

questions.text: What have you tried so far, such as rest, ice, pain relievers, or physical therapy, and did it help?
questions.rationale: Prior response to treatment informs next steps.

questions.text: How is this affecting your sleep, work, or daily activities?
questions.rationale: Functional impact guides urgency and treatment planning.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Cannot bear weight or use limb after injury
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report they cannot put weight on the limb or use it after an injury?

red_flags.label: Visible deformity or audible pop
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe a deformed limb, or hearing or feeling a snap or pop at injury?

red_flags.label: Hot swollen joint with fever
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe a single hot, swollen, painful joint together with fever or chills?

red_flags.label: Back pain with saddle numbness or bladder/bowel change
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report saddle numbness, new loss of bladder or bowel control, or progressive leg weakness?

red_flags.label: Cold, pale, or pulseless limb
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe a limb that is cold, pale, blue, or has lost sensation or pulse?

red_flags.label: Night pain with cancer history or weight loss
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report pain that wakes them at night or is constant, with weight loss or a history of cancer?

red_flags.label: New or worsening weakness
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report arm or leg weakness that is new or getting worse?
